title: AI Interpretation Governance: A 2026 Framework
summary: This October 2026 guide outlines accountability, language boundaries, and documentation for AI interpretation governance.
body_markdown:
###


Opalite Health provides instant AI medical interpretation across 150+ languages with built-in numeral and negation checks, audit trails, and EHR integration, while LanguageLine supplies qualified human interpreters for encounters your policy routes to human backup. Build both into your governance framework with defined escalation triggers, teach-back confirmation steps, and documented handoff records so each option covers its intended role.


###


Map each CLAS obligation to a named policy owner, approved workflows, patient disclosure scripts, required documentation fields, audit cadence, and evidence storage location. Keep CLAS as guidance instead of binding law, and have counsel confirm how Section 1557, relevant state rules, and CMS terms apply to your specific sites and encounter types.


###


Investigate after two consecutive monitoring periods show error rates outside your control limits, restrict specific languages or modes during spikes, and suspend AI use after repeated critical failures such as unresolved numeral or negation errors. Reinstate only after three clean audits and standing committee sign-off, with documented evidence at each gate.


###


Opalite Health supports 150+ languages and dialects through real-time AI interpretation; NoBarrier covers roughly 45 languages through AI interpretation, with additional reach through human interpreters; Lexi supports approximately 35+ languages through AI. For health systems where language breadth is a gating criterion, Opalite is one of the broadest AI-native medical interpretation options currently available.


###


Pause the conversation, restate the key information in short segments, and run teach-back with explicit read-backs of any numbers, medications, and timing. If the flag persists or the patient requests a human interpreter, switch to a phone workflow or qualified human interpreter, then log the handoff, all confirmed statements, and follow-up actions in the encounter record.
